blocks.title: Particulate matter
blocks.text: Particulate matter refers to the wide variety of tiny substances that float in the air as solid particles, liquid droplets or both: all the dust, smoke and haze particles suspended in ambient air, comprising acids, organic chemicals, metals and soil or dust particles.

Sources are both natural and anthropogenic. Natural sources include volcanoes, fires, dust storms and aerosolised sea salt; man-made sources include combustion in mechanical and industrial processes, vehicle emissions and tobacco smoke.

blocks.prompt: Distinguish PM10 from PM2.5 and explain why PM2.5 is more harmful (exercise Q.2i; MCQ III).
blocks.explanation: PM10 is particulate matter up to 10 micrometres across; PM2.5 is the fine fraction up to 2.5 micrometres. The finer particles stay airborne longer, pass the nose and throat and penetrate deep into the lung alveoli and even the bloodstream, so PM2.5 causes more inflammation, heart and lung disease than the coarser PM10.

items: PM: suspended solid particles and liquid droplets (dust, smoke, haze; acids, organics, metals, soil); natural (volcanoes, fires, dust storms, sea salt) and man-made (combustion, vehicles, tobacco smoke).
